cluster_009fe542c789_188283f195d5.headline: Blackstone's BXDC Data Center REIT Raises $1.75B in NYSE IPO
cluster_009fe542c789_188283f195d5.summary: Blackstone Digital Infrastructure Trust (BXDC) completed its NYSE IPO on May 14, raising $1.75 billion by selling 87.5 million shares at $20 per share, with underwriters holding a 30-day option to increase total proceeds to $2 billion. The REIT, structured as a blind pool with no assets yet acquired, will target newly constructed, stabilized data centers valued between $250 million and $1.5 billion, occupied by investment-grade hyperscale tenants on long-term leases at yields of 5.75% to 7%. Blackstone has identified approximately $25 billion in potential near-term acquisitions across Northern Virginia, Ohio, Phoenix, Maryland, and Austin. Nick Pell, former president and CIO of Blackstone's Link Logistics industrial REIT, was named CEO of the new entity.

cluster_7bc83cd4c0f8_e712eb8b2d13.headline: US Industrial Production Jumps 0.7% in April, Best Gain in 14 Months
cluster_7bc83cd4c0f8_e712eb8b2d13.summary: U.S. industrial production rose 0.7% in April 2026, the strongest monthly gain in 14 months and more than double the consensus forecast of 0.3%, according to Federal Reserve G.17 data released May 15. Manufacturing output, which comprises roughly 78% of total industrial production, climbed 0.6%, beating expectations of 0.2%. Utilities output surged 1.9%, while mining output edged down 0.1%. Capacity utilization rose to 76.1%, though it remains 3.3 percentage points below its long-run average.

cluster_e16c7704eeed_f2bb4ff27cfe.headline: Trump and Xi Agree on Strategic Framework, Boeing Deal in Beijing Summit
cluster_e16c7704eeed_f2bb4ff27cfe.summary: President Trump concluded a two-day summit with President Xi Jinping in Beijing on May 15, with China agreeing to purchase U.S. oil and 200 Boeing aircraft. The two leaders established a 'strategic stability' framework to govern the bilateral relationship for three years, with Trump extending an invitation for Xi to visit the White House on September 24. The existing one-year trade truce, set in October 2025, remains in place with average U.S. tariffs on Chinese goods at 47.5%, while the current trade status quo is set to expire in November. Both sides agreed the Strait of Hormuz must remain open for global energy flows, though analysts noted major sticking points including semiconductors and AI remain unresolved.

cluster_8ea3de03d67d_dcb8c8421ec8.headline: Treasury Yields Surge to Multi-Year Highs as Inflation Data Mounts
cluster_8ea3de03d67d_dcb8c8421ec8.summary: U.S. 10-year Treasury yields rose approximately 12-14 basis points to around 4.6% on May 15, while 30-year yields climbed to roughly 5.12%, the highest level since 2007, amid a broad global bond selloff. Import prices rose 1.9% in April and 4.2% on a 12-month basis — the largest annual gain since October 2022 — while export prices surged 8.8%, the highest since September 2022. Oil prices added to inflation pressures, with West Texas Intermediate rising to approximately $104 per barrel and Brent crude surpassing $107 per barrel, driven by an unresolved Strait of Hormuz standoff, pushing national gas prices above $4.50 per gallon — up 51% since the Iran war began. Newly confirmed Fed Chair Kevin Warsh, narrowly approved by the Senate this week, faces the market turmoil as his first major test, with traders now pricing a near two-thirds probability of a Fed rate hike in December.

cluster_63256dcd157d_8ea3de03d67d_dcb8c8.headline: Treasury Yields Surge Past 4.6% as Inflation Data Hits 2022 Highs
cluster_63256dcd157d_8ea3de03d67d_dcb8c8.summary: U.S. 10-year Treasury yields rose roughly 12-14 basis points to approximately 4.6% on May 15, with 30-year yields climbing to 5.12%, the highest level since 2007, amid accelerating consumer and wholesale price data. Import prices rose 4.2% on a 12-month basis — the largest annual gain since October 2022 — while export prices surged 8.8%, the highest since September 2022. Brent crude climbed past $107 per barrel and WTI rose to $104.39, driven by an unresolved Strait of Hormuz standoff following the Iran war, with national gas prices holding above $4.50 per gallon — up 51% since the conflict began. Money markets priced a near-zero probability of Fed rate cuts in 2025 and roughly a 50-65% chance of a December rate hike, marking the first major test for newly confirmed Fed Chair Kevin Warsh as the S&P 500 fell more than 1% on the session.

cluster_62493c4ebe5e_d2ec57b03369.headline: G-7 Finance Ministers in Paris Confront Global Bond Market Selloff
cluster_62493c4ebe5e_d2ec57b03369.summary: G-7 finance ministers convened in Paris on May 18 amid a deepening global bond selloff driven by investor fears over oil-fueled inflation linked to the US-Iran conflict and the Strait of Hormuz closure. The 30-year US Treasury yield reached its highest level since 2007, while German 30-year debt hit its loftiest level in 15 years. French Finance Minister Roland Lescure described the market moves as a correction rather than a collapse, stating that public debt is 'no longer an irrelevant policy topic.' The bond market turmoil overshadowed the ministers' scheduled agenda, which included discussions of US fiscal deficits, China's trade surpluses, and European underinvestment.

cluster_46554e071e5c_99e60bbf62d9.headline: BUILD America 250 Act Sets AV Framework, Revises Broker and Safety Rules
cluster_46554e071e5c_99e60bbf62d9.summary: The BUILD America 250 Act establishes the first federal regulatory framework for autonomous commercial trucks, requiring the Department of Transportation to develop safety standards within two years, while stopping short of authorizing immediate deployment. The legislation also revises freight broker qualification requirements, overhauling the DataQs process for disputing safety violations and setting a federal timeline for hair follicle drug testing of commercial drivers. Liability questions for autonomous vehicles would remain subject to jury determination under the bill. Additional provisions include funding for workforce retraining programs tied to the autonomous trucking transition, with broader implications for broker licensing standards, motor carrier compliance, and insurance renewal cycles.

cluster_0addadd38041_27c99f3c1251_7e0df1.headline: China Commits $17B Annually in U.S. Farm Goods, 200 Boeing Jets After Trump-Xi Summit
cluster_0addadd38041_27c99f3c1251_7e0df1.summary: China agreed to purchase at least $17 billion per year in U.S. agricultural products for 2026, 2027, and 2028, plus 25 million metric tons of soybeans annually, totaling roughly $27 billion per year in agricultural commitments. China also approved an initial order of 200 American-made Boeing aircraft, the first such commitment since 2017, and will restore market access for U.S. beef by relisting more than 400 U.S. beef facilities while resuming poultry imports from USDA-certified bird-flu-free states. The two countries established a U.S.-China Board of Trade and a U.S.-China Board of Investment as the cornerstone of the agreement, with the trade board potentially facilitating tariff reductions on some $30 billion in non-sensitive goods. China additionally agreed to address U.S. concerns over supply chain shortages of rare earth minerals including yttrium, scandium, neodymium, and indium, though both sides characterized the summit outcomes as preliminary with further negotiations expected.
